welcome.title: Welcome to Voice Generator
welcome.description: Turn any text into natural-sounding speech in seconds. Pick a voice, type what you want it to say, fine-tune how it sounds, and generate — it's that simple.

tips.0: No recording or audio editing experience needed
tips.1: Follow the 4-step process: Voice → Prompt → Settings → Generate
tips.2: Preview and download the result directly from the player

voice.title: Step 1 — Select a Voice
voice.description: Choose the voice that will speak your text. Each voice has its own tone, accent, and character — browse the list and pick the one that fits your content best.

tips.0: Listen to previews before committing to a voice
tips.1: Match the voice gender and tone to your target audience
tips.2: Narration voices work best for long-form content like articles or stories
tips.3: Conversational voices feel more natural for short messages or dialogue

prompt.title: Step 2 — Enter Your Text
prompt.description: Type or paste the text you want the voice to speak. The AI will read it exactly as written, so punctuation and sentence structure directly affect the delivery.

tips.0: Use commas and periods to control natural pauses in speech
tips.1: Write numbers and abbreviations in full for better pronunciation
tips.2: Keep sentences concise — shorter sentences sound more natural
tips.3: Use exclamation marks or question marks to influence tone and inflection

settings.title: Step 3 — Adjust Voice Settings
settings.description: Fine-tune three parameters that shape how the voice sounds: Stability controls consistency, Similarity controls how closely it matches the original voice, and Style Strength sets how expressive the delivery is.

tips.0: Stability: higher = more consistent and monotone, lower = more varied and expressive
tips.1: Similarity: higher = closer to the original voice sample, lower = more flexible interpretation
tips.2: Style Strength: higher = more dramatic and emotional delivery, lower = neutral and calm
tips.3: Start with default values and adjust one parameter at a time

generate.title: Generate Your Voice
generate.description: Once your voice, text, and settings are ready, hit Generate. The AI will synthesize the audio in seconds — preview it in the player and download when you're happy with the result.

tips.0: Generation typically completes in just a few seconds
tips.1: Preview the audio before downloading to check pacing and tone
tips.2: Not satisfied? Adjust stability or style strength and regenerate
tips.3: Try the same text with different voices to find the best match

generate.subtitle: Your audio is ready to play

QuickTips.title: Quick Tips
QuickTips.footer: Experiment with different voices and settings to find what works best for your content!

tip1.title: Write Naturally
tip1.description: Write your script the way you'd speak it. Natural, conversational phrasing produces better-sounding audio than stiff formal text.

tip2.title: Pick the Right Voice
tip2.description: Preview each voice before committing. Match tone, gender, and accent to your target audience for the best result.

tip3.title: Use Punctuation for Pacing
tip3.description: Commas and periods create natural pauses in speech. A well-punctuated script gives you precise control over the delivery rhythm.

tip4.title: Adjust Stability
tip4.description: Lower stability adds expressiveness and variation between takes. Higher stability makes the voice more consistent — great for professional narration.

tip5.title: Style Strength
tip5.description: Boost Style Strength for emotional or dramatic delivery. Keep it low for a neutral, clean voiceover that works in any context.

tip6.title: Batch Your Segments

welcome.title: Welcome to TrendYuu Studio
welcome.description: TrendYuu Studio lets you generate original AI music tracks from text prompts. Describe the mood, genre, instruments, and style — and get a unique track in seconds.

tips.0: Works best with Creator or Pro plans.
tips.1: Each generation costs 550 credits.
tips.2: Your tracks are saved to your gallery automatically.

prompt.title: Writing Your Prompt
prompt.description: The prompt is the heart of your music generation. Be descriptive — include genre, mood, tempo, instruments, and any reference artists or vibes you want.

tips.0: Example: "Chill lo-fi hip hop, slow tempo, piano and vinyl crackle, rainy day mood".
tips.1: Mention BPM or energy level for more precise results.
tips.2: Reference specific instruments or soundscapes for best results.

filename.title: Custom Filename (Optional)
filename.description: You can give your track a custom name before generating. This makes it easier to find in your gallery later. If left blank, a name will be auto-generated.

tips.0: Use descriptive names like "intro-chill-loop" to stay organised.
tips.1: The .mp3 extension is added automatically.
tips.2: Rename anytime from your gallery.

negative.title: Negative Prompt (Optional)
negative.description: Use the negative prompt to exclude elements you don't want in your track — specific instruments, genres, or characteristics that clash with your vision.

tips.0: Example: "no drums, no distortion, no vocals".
tips.1: Keep it short and specific — a few keywords work best.
tips.2: Combine with a strong positive prompt for the most control.

generate.title: Generate & Listen
generate.description: Hit Generate and the AI will compose your track. You'll see it appear in the Tracks list with a live progress indicator. Once complete, you can play, download, or remove it.

tips.0: Generation typically takes 15–45 seconds.
tips.1: You can queue another generation while one is in progress.
tips.2: Download your track as a .mp3 file to use in any DAW or video editor.

QuickTips.title: Quick Tips
QuickTips.footer: Experiment freely — every prompt gives a unique result. The more specific your description, the closer the output matches your vision.

tip1.title: Be Descriptive
tip1.description: Include genre, mood, instruments, and tempo in your prompt. The more detail you give, the closer the output will be to what you have in mind.

tip2.title: Name Your Genres
tip2.description: Mention specific subgenres like "lo-fi hip hop", "dark techno", or "spaghetti western" instead of just "electronic" or "music" for sharper results.

tip3.title: Layer Moods & Instruments
tip3.description: Combine emotional descriptors with instrument names — e.g. "melancholic piano, sparse drums, tape hiss" — to sculpt a very specific sonic palette.

tip4.title: Use Negative Prompts
tip4.description: Exclude elements that don't fit your vision. Adding "no vocals, no distortion" in the negative prompt field helps steer the AI away from unwanted characteristics.

tip5.title: Reference Tempo & Energy
tip5.description: Add BPM hints like "slow 70 BPM" or energy descriptors like "high energy, driving rhythm" to shape how the track feels rhythmically.

tip6.title: Iterate Quickly
tip6.description: Generate multiple variations by tweaking one or two words at a time. Small changes — like swapping "warm" for "cold" — can dramatically change the output.

step0.title: Welcome to Ninja
step0.description: Cards fly up from the bottom of the screen. Your goal is to slice as many as possible before they fall out of frame — without letting them escape or hitting a bomb. The higher your combo, the more points each slice is worth.
tips: Cards speed up as your score increases — stay alert.
Cards sometimes spawn in groups — prepare for bursts.
Your high score is saved automatically after each game.

step1.title: How to Play
step1.description: Click (or tap on mobile) and drag across cards to slice them. Your blade is your cursor trail — the faster you swipe, the more satisfying the cut. You can slice multiple cards in a single drag.
tips: On mobile, swipe quickly across the screen with your finger.
Long diagonal swipes let you catch several cards at once.
Press P on keyboard to pause and resume the game.

step2.title: Normal Cards
step2.description: Scissors cards (✂️) are the most common type. They appear in five different colors — pink, amber, violet, cyan, and emerald — but all behave the same way. Slice them to earn +100 points each.
tips: Missing a normal card costs you one life.
Each color is equally common — no hidden differences.
Normal cards are worth more when your combo multiplier is active.

step3.title: Special Cards
step3.description: Five unique card types change the game when sliced — or hit by accident. Learn to recognise them at a glance so you can react in time.
tips: 🏆 Bonus — Worth +300 pts. Rare golden card.
✨ Special — Worth +500 pts and activates 2× mode for 5 seconds.
➕ Healing — Restores one lost life. Prioritise these when low.
⚡ Thunder — Clears every card on screen instantly. Safe to use when overwhelmed.
💣 Bomb — Slicing it costs a life and resets your combo. Avoid!

step4.title: Combos & Multipliers
step4.description: Slice cards within 1.5 seconds of each other to build a combo chain. The longer your streak, the higher your score multiplier climbs — up to 4× for 10 or more consecutive slices.
tips: 4+ combo → 2× multiplier
7+ combo → 3× multiplier
10+ combo → 4× multiplier — your most valuable window.
Hitting a bomb resets the combo chain immediately.
step4.visualTip: Slice cards within 1.5s to build combos

step5.title: Lives & Special Mode
step5.description: You start with 3 lives shown as red circles in the top-right. You lose a life when a normal or bonus card exits the screen, or when you slice a bomb. Reach 0 and the game ends.
tips: Prioritise healing cards (➕) to get lives back.
Special mode (✨) doubles all points for 5 seconds — save your biggest combo for it.
The thunder card (⚡) is great panic-button when too many cards appear at once.

step0.title: Welcome to Jumper
step0.description: A side-scrolling runner where obstacles charge at you from the right. Jump over ground barriers, duck under flying ones, and survive as long as you can. The game never ends — it just gets faster.
tips: There are no lives — one hit ends the run.
Your score climbs automatically while you're alive.
Your high score is saved after every run.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: On desktop use the arrow keys or Space to jump, and hold the Down arrow to duck. On mobile, the ▲ and ▼ buttons at the bottom of the game work the same way. You can also tap the canvas itself to jump.
tips: Space and ↑ both trigger a jump — use whichever feels natural.
Hold ↓ (or hold ▼) to stay ducked — releasing it stands you back up.
On mobile, tap the canvas anywhere to jump when no duck is needed.

step2.title: Your Character
step2.description: You play as the cyan square. It has three states: standing at full height, ducked to half height, and airborne. Knowing your exact hitbox in each state is key — collisions have a small 8px margin of forgiveness.
tips: Your hitbox is slightly smaller than the sprite — use it to your advantage.
You can only jump while standing on the ground, not while already airborne.
Ducking while jumping won't lower your height — land first, then duck.

step3.title: Ground Obstacles
step3.description: Pink barriers rise from the ground in random heights ranging from short stumps to tall walls. Short ones can be cleared with a normal jump. Taller ones require you to time your jump earlier and arc over them cleanly.
tips: Jump as soon as you spot a tall barrier — don't wait.
Short barriers only need a quick tap of the jump key.
You cannot duck under ground obstacles — you must jump over them.

step4.title: Flying Obstacles
step4.description: Orange barriers float at various heights with a gap at the bottom. Duck and hold to slide underneath them. The gap is always large enough for your ducked hitbox — but you must keep holding the duck key until you're fully clear.
tips: Start ducking early — you need to be low before reaching the barrier.
Hold the duck key until the obstacle is completely behind you.
Some flying barriers are placed low; others have a generous gap — read ahead.

step5.title: Speed & Scoring
step5.description: Your score ticks up continuously while you're alive. Every 10 points, obstacles move faster and spawn more frequently. The background colour also shifts every 50 points — a visual cue that things are about to get harder.
tips: Speed increases are gradual — stay calm and read each obstacle early.
There's no score cap — see how far you can push it.
At very high scores obstacles can spawn in pairs — expect back-to-back reads.
step5.visualTip1: Speed and spawn rate increase every 10 points

step0.title: Welcome to Pong
step0.description: The classic paddle game. A ball bounces between two paddles — yours on the left (green) and the opponent on the right (red). Let the ball get past your paddle and the enemy scores. Get it past theirs and you score.
tips: Play vs CPU solo or pass the keyboard to a friend in Local mode.
There's no round limit — play until you stop.
Your high score is only tracked in CPU mode.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: In CPU mode you control the left (green) paddle using W/S or the arrow keys — both work at the same time. In Local 2-player mode, Player 1 uses W/S and Player 2 uses the arrow keys. On mobile, use the ▲▼ buttons at the bottom of each side.
tips: W/S and ↑/↓ are interchangeable in CPU mode — use whichever is comfortable.
In Local mode, both players must share the keyboard.
Mobile buttons highlight pink when pressed so you can confirm input.

step2.title: Paddles & Ball
step2.description: The green paddle is yours, the red paddle is the CPU (or Player 2). The yellow ball bounces off the top and bottom walls and off the face of each paddle. Hitting the ball with the edge of your paddle adds a slight angle to the return.
tips: Try to hit the ball with the edge of your paddle to make it harder to return.
The ball bounces at a predictable angle off walls — anticipate where it will end up.
Goal boxes on each side mark the danger zone — keep the ball out of yours.

step3.title: Scoring
step3.description: You score a point when the ball passes the right side of the screen (behind the red paddle). The CPU scores when it passes the left side. After each point, the ball resets to the centre and fires toward the player who just lost the point.
tips: After conceding, the ball comes straight at you — be ready immediately.
There is no win condition — the game continues indefinitely.
Your leaderboard score is your highest player score reached in a session.

step4.title: Ball Speed
step4.description: Every time the ball hits a paddle, it speeds up by 5%. This resets when a point is scored. Long rallies can get very fast — the key is staying centred and reacting early rather than chasing the ball.
tips: Stay near the centre of the court vertically to cut off more angles.
During long rallies, watch the ball's trajectory from further away, not just its current position.
Scoring breaks the speed buildup — use aggressive play to force the reset.
step4.speedDesc: +5% speed per paddle hit — resets when a point is scored

step5.title: Difficulty
step5.description: In CPU mode, choose Easy, Medium, or Hard before starting. Difficulty affects how fast the AI moves, how accurately it tracks the ball, and how quickly it reacts. Difficulty cannot be changed mid-game and is disabled in Local 2-player mode.
tips: Easy: the AI is slow and aims poorly — great for practicing rallies.
Medium: a fair challenge with some reaction delay and positional error.
Hard: the AI moves fast, reacts quickly, and barely misses — requires precise play.
step5.difficultyDesc: Difficulty only applies in CPU mode — not available in local 2-player

step0.title: Welcome to Snake
step0.description: Guide your pink snake around the grid to eat red food pellets. Each pellet you eat makes the snake one segment longer. The game ends if you crash into a wall or into your own body — unless a wrap mode is active.
tips: The goal is to eat as many pellets as possible without crashing.
Winning means filling the entire board — it's rare, so aim for a high score.
Your leaderboard score accounts for both pellets eaten and how fast you played.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Use WASD or the arrow keys to steer the snake. On mobile, use the D-pad buttons that appear below the game. The snake moves on a fixed tick — inputs are queued, so you can press two directions quickly to turn a corner in one tick.
tips: WASD and arrow keys work simultaneously — use whichever feels natural.
You can't reverse directly into yourself — that input is ignored.
Queue two turns in quick succession to take tight corners without slowing down.

step2.title: Food & Scoring
step2.description: Each red pellet you eat scores +10 points and adds one segment to your snake's tail. The snake's head is bright pink, and the body is darker pink — use the head as your reference point when navigating. A new pellet appears on a random empty cell after each eat.
tips: Plan your path to the food while also leaving yourself an escape route.
The longer your snake, the fewer empty cells exist for food to spawn.
Eating quickly earns a higher time multiplier when you win — don't dawdle.

step3.title: Wrap Modes
step3.description: Choose a wrap mode before starting. Classic: hitting any wall is instant death. Full Warp: the snake passes through walls and re-enters from the opposite side. Random Warp: four portals appear as gaps in the border — entering one teleports you to a random other portal.
tips: Classic is the most challenging since walls are always lethal.
Full Warp is great for higher scores since you can use the edges freely.
In Random Warp, learn where the portals are before committing to a path near the border.
step3.randomWarpDesc: Portals in the border — enter one, exit another

step4.title: Speed & Time Multiplier
step4.description: The snake starts slow (speed 4) and gets faster by 0.25 with every pellet eaten, capping at speed 12. If you win by filling the board, your final score is multiplied by a time bonus — the faster you complete the run, the higher the multiplier (up to 4×).
tips: The time multiplier only applies when you win — it has no effect on game-over scores.
At max speed the snake moves three times faster than the start — plan further ahead.
A slow, methodical win still scores 1× — speed runs reward aggressive play.

step5.title: Winning
step5.description: You win when there are no empty cells left for food to spawn — meaning your snake has filled the entire board. The game then shows your score multiplied by the time bonus. It's a rare achievement, especially on Classic mode.
tips: Use a systematic back-and-forth (boustrophedon) path to fill the board safely.
Avoid cutting yourself off from sections of the board as your snake grows.
Full Warp mode makes winning significantly easier since walls are no longer obstacles.

step0.title: Welcome to Space Shooter
step0.description: Pilot your pink ship through waves of red enemies. Shoot automatically — your only job is to dodge bullets, collect power-ups, and survive boss encounters every 5th wave. The game runs indefinitely; your score is your record.
tips: Your ship fires continuously — no need to press anything to shoot.
A boss appears every 5th wave. Bosses are worth +200 points each.
Your high score is saved automatically when a game session ends.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Move with the arrow keys. Press Shift to Dodge — you move at 2× speed and are temporarily invincible (2 second cooldown). Press Space to use a Bomb — it destroys all enemies and bullets on screen. On mobile, use the virtual joystick and the Dodge/Bomb buttons.
tips: Dodge is your most important tool — save it for dense bullet patterns.
Bombs start with 2 — collect Bomb pickups (!) to restock up to 3.
The joystick on mobile mirrors the arrow keys in real time.

step2.title: Enemies & Waves
step2.description: Every 4 seconds a new wave of enemies spawns. There are 24 different formation patterns — straight lines, V formations, spirals, side sweeps, pincer attacks, and more. Each enemy fires back at you periodically. Clearing enemies by flying into them also works but costs a life.
tips: Stay near the centre of the screen to respond quickly to any angle.
Enemy bullets are orange — distinguish them from your pink bullets.
After wave 5 the formation pool reshuffles — expect harder variants.

step3.title: Power-ups
step3.description: Pickups fall from above and drift down slowly. Fly into them to collect. Each type is colour-coded with a letter: B (Boost) = faster fire rate for 5s · M (Multishot) = extra bullet lanes (stacks to 6 levels) · + (Life) = restore one life · S (Shield) = absorb hits for 10s · ! (Bomb) = gain one bomb · » (Speed) = 1.5× movement for 6s · $ (Money) = +25 points.
tips: Multishot stacks — each M pickup adds a full level, up to 9 simultaneous bullets.
Shield does not stack with Dodge — the Dodge invincibility always takes priority.
$ pickups are the most common — grab them freely for easy score padding.

step4.title: Defence & Lives
step4.description: You start with 3 lives (pink triangles, top-right). Hitting an enemy or bullet costs one life and grants 2 seconds of invincibility (the ship blinks). Shield (green aura) absorbs hits without life loss. Dodge (blue aura) makes you invincible and doubles your speed for 0.15 seconds.
tips: After taking damage you have 2s of free movement — use it to reposition.
Shield absorbs contact with enemies too, not just bullets.
You can hold up to 4 lives with a Life (+) pickup when already at 3.

step5.title: Scoring
step5.description: Each regular enemy killed is worth +10 points. Each boss killed is worth +200 points. Money pickups ($) give +25. Bomb-clearing a full wave of 10 enemies gives +50 points. There is no time bonus or multiplier — pure kill count wins.
tips: Prioritise killing enemies over dodging when your score multiplier is high.
Don't waste bombs on small waves — save them for dense swarms or boss bullet storms.
Multishot level 6 (9 bullets) makes bosses significantly faster to kill.

boss0.title: Boss 0 — Spread
boss0.description: The Spread Boss fires a fan of 3 bullets in phase 1, expanding to 5 bullets in phase 2. The fan is centred downward, so staying directly below it is the most dangerous position. It turns red/dark-red below 25% HP and accelerates.
tips: Stay to one side of the fan rather than directly below.
The fire rate increases in phase 2 — start saving your Dodge for this.
This is the most common first boss — a good warm-up for the others.

boss1.title: Boss 1 — Circular
boss1.description: The Circular Boss fires a ring of 8 bullets in all directions, expanding to 12 in phase 2. The ring is omnidirectional — there's no safe angle, only safe distance. Move sideways to slip between the gaps in the ring.
tips: Stay at mid-range — close enough to hit it, far enough to read the gaps.
Move perpendicular to the ring, not away from it, to find gaps.
In phase 2, the gaps narrow significantly — be ready to Dodge through.

boss2.title: Boss 2 — Tracking
boss2.description: The Tracking Boss aims every shot directly at your current position. In phase 1 it fires one bullet per burst; phase 2 fires three in a spread. The bullet speed is medium — you can dodge predictably by moving in a wide arc.
tips: Move continuously — staying still is instant death with this boss.
Move in slow circular arcs; sharp turns are harder to read.
In phase 2 the triple spread means the centre shot is always aimed — dodge sideways.

boss3.title: Boss 3 — Spiral
boss3.description: The Spiral Boss fires a single bullet per tick in a continuously rotating direction, creating a spinning bullet spiral across the whole arena. The spiral is slow but fills the screen over time. Weave through the gaps as they rotate past you.
tips: Follow the direction of the spiral rather than fighting against it.
Don't rush to kill it — panicked movement breaks your weave rhythm.
In phase 2 the spiral spins faster — begin positioning earlier between gaps.

boss4.title: Boss 4 — Wave
boss4.description: The Wave Boss fires 3 oscillating columns of bullets in phase 1 and 5 in phase 2. The horizontal offset of each bullet shifts like a sine wave, making the columns sweep left and right unpredictably. Time your movement to pass through the opening between columns.
tips: Watch the column ends, not the midpoints — the ends give you the clearest read.
Moving left-right in sync with the wave's rhythm helps you stay in the gaps.
Phase 2 adds two extra columns — the safe corridor becomes much narrower.

boss5.title: Boss 5 — Barrage
boss5.description: The Barrage Boss fires a wide fan of 6 bullets in a single burst in phase 1 and 10 in phase 2, but with a longer cooldown between bursts. The long pause lets you position aggressively, but the burst is wide enough to cover most of the screen.
tips: Use the long cooldown to move close and deal maximum DPS.
The moment you see the burst fire, Dodge through it.
Phase 2 fan is nearly 120° — position yourself off-centre to have fewer bullets to dodge.

boss6.title: Boss 6 — Mirror
boss6.description: The Mirror Boss fires two aimed bullets simultaneously from the left and right edges of its body — they always converge on your position from two angles. In phase 2 it also fires a slow centre beam straight down. This butterfly-shaped boss requires you to commit to one side.
tips: Pick one side (left or right) and stay there — trying to thread the middle gets you hit by both.
The centre beam in phase 2 is slow — move away laterally as soon as it fires.
The mirrored shots are aimed, so sudden direction changes can cause both to miss.

boss7.title: Boss 7 — Sniper
boss7.description: The Sniper Boss has a long cooldown but fires 2 highly accurate bullets in a burst (4 in phase 2). The bullets have a slight jitter so they're not perfectly precise — but they're fast. The long thin cross shape telegraphs charge-up. Move immediately when you see it shoot.
tips: The long cooldown means you get plenty of time to deal damage — stay aggressive.
Move laterally at the moment of firing — the slight jitter means sideways dodges always work.
Phase 2 fires 4 bullets in a tight spread — one lateral dodge still clears all of them.

boss8.title: Boss 8 — Swarm
boss8.description: The Swarm Boss fires a single random low-speed bullet every 0.08 seconds — an extremely rapid but unpredictable spray. Individually each bullet is easy to dodge, but the volume builds up quickly. The spiky lime-green shape is distinctive; prioritise killing it fast.
tips: Move in large sweeping S-curves to avoid accumulation of random bullets.
This boss rewards aggressive play — the faster it dies, the less spray you face.
Bombs are effective here as the bullet density from this boss fills the screen in phase 2.

boss9.title: Boss 9 — Cross Cannon
boss9.description: The Cross Cannon Boss fires in 4 cardinal directions simultaneously and the entire pattern slowly rotates over time. In phase 2 it fires 8 directions. The rotation speed is about one full turn every 8 seconds — fast enough that static positions become dangerous.
tips: Rotate with the cannon — move in a slow circle matching the pattern's rotation.
Avoid camping in a fixed corner since the rotating pattern will catch you.
Phase 2 adds 4 diagonal shots making it nearly impossible to stay in one safe spot — keep moving.

step0.title: Welcome to Tetris
step0.description: Falling pieces called tetrominoes drop from the top of the board. Stack them to fill complete horizontal lines — cleared lines score points and keep the board from filling up. Survive as long as possible and aim for the highest score!
tips: The game ends when pieces stack above the top of the board.
A ghost piece (dashed outline) shows exactly where your piece will land.
Speed increases every 500 points — plan ahead as things heat up.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Move pieces left and right, rotate them, and soft-drop to speed up their fall. On mobile use the on-screen D-pad; on desktop use arrow keys or WASD. The ⇄ button swaps the current piece into the Hold slot.
tips: ← / → (or A / D) — move the piece sideways.
↺ (or ↑ / W) — rotate the piece 90° clockwise.
▼ (or ↓ / S) — soft-drop: fall faster while held.

step2.title: The 7 Tetrominoes
step2.description: Classic mode uses the 7 standard pieces, each named after the letter it resembles. Learning each shape's rotation states is key to placing them cleanly and building flat stacks.
tips: The I-piece is the only one that can clear 4 lines at once (a 'Tetris').
The O-piece doesn't change when rotated — use it to plug square gaps.
S and Z pieces are the trickiest — try to keep them near the edges.

step3.title: Game Modes
step3.description: Three modes change which pieces can appear. Classic uses the 7 standard tetrominoes. Chaos adds 4 irregular shapes that are harder to place. Pentomino introduces 7 five-cell pieces for expert-level stacking.
tips: Select your mode before pressing Play — it can't be changed mid-game.
Chaos and Pentomino pieces are wider/taller, so keep the centre clear.
Master Classic first before tackling the harder modes.

step4.title: Scoring & Combos
step4.description: Points are awarded per line clear, multiplied by the current level. Clear multiple lines in a single placement for bigger rewards — a Tetris (4 lines) scores 800 × level. Chain consecutive clears within 1.5 s to build a combo multiplier for even more points!
tips: 4-line Tetris clears give 8× more points than clearing 1 line four times.
Each combo step adds ×0.5 to your score multiplier — chains pay off fast.
Level rises every 500 points, making pieces fall faster and scoring higher.

step5.title: Hold Piece & Ghost
step5.description: The Hold slot lets you save a piece for later — swap it back in any time you need a specific shape. The ghost piece (dashed outline) shows the exact landing position so you can place pieces confidently without guessing.
tips: Hold can only be used once per piece — it resets after the piece lands.
Save the I-piece in Hold and drop it in when a 4-line gap is ready.
Toggle the ghost piece off in the header if you prefer a challenge.

visuals.controlsHint: Position the plate under falling blocks
visuals.comboDescription: Land Good or Perfect placements in a row to build a combo. Each adds +10 pts × combo count.
visuals.comboReset: Combo resets on miss or bad landing!
visuals.physicsDescription: If the tower leans too far, it collapses — game over!
visuals.modeStickyDesc: Blocks attach firmly. Great for beginners.
visuals.modeDynamicDesc: Blocks react to plate movement. +25% pts!

step0.title: Welcome to Stack Builder
step0.description: Blocks fall from above — move your plate to catch them and build the tallest tower you can. The higher your stack, the further the camera scrolls up, taking you from a city skyline all the way into space!
tips: Blocks that fall off the plate cost you a life — you only have 3.
The camera follows your tower upward as it grows.
The background shifts from city to stars the higher you stack.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Move the plate left and right to position it under the falling block. On desktop you can use arrow keys, WASD, or the mouse. On mobile use the on-screen ◄ ► buttons.
tips: ← / → or A / D — hold to continuously slide the plate.
Mouse move — the plate follows your cursor directly.
Mobile ◄ ► buttons — hold for smooth continuous movement.

step2.title: Alignment & Scoring
step2.description: Where the block lands on the plate determines your score. A perfect center landing is worth 100 pts, a near miss 50, and an edge catch 25. Miss entirely and you lose a life with no points.
tips: Perfect (center zone, ~6px) = 100 pts per block.
Good (near zone, ~18px) = 50 pts — also builds your combo.
Edge catch = 25 pts but resets your combo streak.

step3.title: Combo Multiplier
step3.description: Land consecutive Perfect or Good placements within 2 seconds of each other to build a combo chain. Each link in the chain awards an extra +10 pts × your current combo count — the longer the chain, the faster points multiply!
tips: Combos reset on any miss, bad landing, or if the 2s timer expires.
A 5-hit combo already adds +50 bonus pts on top of the landing score.
Focus on positioning accuracy rather than speed to keep chains alive.

step4.title: Tower Balance & Physics
step4.description: Your tower has real tilt physics. If too many blocks are placed off-center, the tower starts to lean. If the lean exceeds a critical angle it topples — and the game ends. Keep your stack as vertical as possible!
tips: Blocks higher up have more leverage — off-center placements near the top tilt harder.
You can see the tilt happening live: compensate by landing the next block on the opposite side.
Dynamic mode makes the plate movement also push on the tower — be gentle.

step5.title: Sticky vs Dynamic Blocks
step5.description: Choose your difficulty before starting. Sticky Blocks mode locks each block firmly to the plate — great for learning. Dynamic Blocks mode lets blocks react to plate momentum, making the tower wobble when you move fast, but rewarding you with a +25% point bonus.
tips: Sticky mode: ideal for learning alignment and building long combos.
Dynamic mode: sudden plate direction changes transfer lateral force to the tower.
In Dynamic mode, small smooth adjustments are safer than rapid slides.

visual.dragTip: Drag ball back, release to launch

visual.dragPan: Drag canvas to pan the view

step0.title: Welcome to Ball Launcher
step0.description: Launch coloured balls from a slingshot to topple structures and squash the green enemies perched on top. Each level introduces taller, more complex arrangements of glass, wood, and stone blocks. Clear every enemy to advance!
tips: The camera pans right at the start to preview the whole level, then returns to the slingshot.
You have a limited number of balls — unused balls score bonus points when the level ends.
Enemies can be knocked off by toppling blocks onto them, not just by direct hits.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Pull the ball backward on the slingshot, aim at your target, and release to fire. A dotted trajectory line shows where the ball will go. On desktop you can also click and drag the canvas to pan the view and scout ahead.
tips: Drag further back for more power — the pull distance directly controls launch speed.
Tap or click the canvas while a ball is mid-flight to activate its special ability.
Use the Skip Ball button to discard a flying ball early if it won't hit anything useful.

step2.title: Obstacles
step2.description: Five block types fill the structures. Glass shatters in one hit. Wood takes two. Stone needs three or more. TNT blocks explode when destroyed, chaining damage to everything nearby. Balloons float upward and can lift cargo with them.
tips: Glass gives only 5 pts but falls apart fastest — use it as a path to reach enemies behind stone.
Stone blocks (25 pts) are the highest value; a Heavy or Bomb ball is best against them.
TNT chain reactions can clear entire structures — aim for centrally placed TNT blocks.

step3.title: Ball Types
step3.description: Seven ball types are available, each with a unique colour and a special ability triggered by tapping during flight. The next ball type is shown below the canvas — its colour tells you at a glance what effect it carries.
tips: Normal (red) has no ability — use it for straightforward direct hits.
Heavy (dark red) deals massively increased damage on impact, especially against stone.
Bouncy (purple) has very high restitution — it caroms wildly and can hit multiple targets.

step4.title: Ball Abilities
step4.description: All balls except Normal and Heavy have an ability that activates when you tap or click during flight — only once per ball. Time your tap for maximum impact: trigger Splitter above a cluster, detonate the Bomb at the heart of a structure, or redirect the Boomerang for a second pass.
tips: Splitter: tap while airborne to burst into 3 smaller balls that fan out through the target.
Bomb: detonates a 150-unit radius explosion at the moment you click — great for dense clusters.
Speed: fires a forward burst; use it when the ball is lined up with a distant enemy.

step5.title: Scoring & Levels
step5.description: Points come from destroying obstacles and enemies. Each level adds more complexity and more enemy clusters. You start with 3 balls and earn an extra ball every 3 levels. If you run out of balls before all enemies are gone, it's game over.
tips: Leftover balls are not currently converted to bonus points — use every ball wisely.
Fall damage is free — topple heavy stone blocks onto enemies below for bonus kills.
TNT chain explosions can award hundreds of points if placed near multiple obstacles and enemies.

visuals.descendWarning: New rows of bricks descend periodically — don't let them reach your paddle!
visuals.dropIntro: Some bricks drop power-ups when destroyed
visuals.levelAdvanceHint: Clear all bricks to advance. More rows spawn each level.

step0.title: Welcome to Brick Breaker
step0.description: A bouncing ball smashes through rows of bricks while you control the paddle below. New rows of bricks descend over time — clear them faster than they fall and rack up the highest score you can before the board overwhelms you!
tips: The ball bounces off walls, bricks, and your paddle.
If all balls fall below the paddle, it's game over.
If any brick row reaches your paddle level, it's also game over.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Slide the paddle left and right to keep the ball in play. On desktop use the arrow keys or move the mouse across the canvas. On mobile use the on-screen ◄ ► buttons.
tips: ← / → arrow keys — hold for continuous movement.
Mouse — the paddle follows your cursor horizontally over the canvas.
Where on the paddle the ball hits changes its bounce angle — use the edges to aim.

step2.title: Bricks & Hit Points
step2.description: Bricks come in different strengths. Standard bricks break in one hit. Orange bricks need two hits and show a number. Purple armored bricks take three or more hits. Higher levels spawn tougher bricks more frequently.
tips: Destroying a brick = 100 pts. Hitting without destroying = 25 pts.
Orange (2 HP) and purple (3+ HP) bricks appear more often at higher levels.
Target clusters of 1-HP bricks first to clear space quickly.

step3.title: Power-Up Drops
step3.description: When a brick is destroyed there is a chance it drops a power-up. Catch it with the paddle before it falls off screen! There are three types: a new extra ball, a ball duplicator, and a paddle extender.
tips: Blue circle — spawns one extra ball from the paddle.
Purple circle — mirrors every current ball, doubling your count.
Green circle — widens the paddle by +15px for 8 seconds (stackable).

step4.title: Difficulty & Levels
step4.description: Pick a difficulty before pressing Play — it cannot be changed mid-game. Easy gives a slow ball and wide timing windows. Hard fires the ball fast with a tight paddle speed. Clear every brick on screen to advance to the next level and earn a 500 pt bonus.
tips: Easy: best for learning the brick patterns and power-up timing.
Hard: faster ball means less reaction time — aim bounces off the edges for control.
Each level adds more rows and bricks — the escalating pace is the real challenge.

step5.title: Scoring & Survival
step5.description: Stack up points by destroying bricks and clearing levels. Your main goal is keeping at least one ball in play while preventing the advancing brick rows from reaching the paddle. Power-ups are your lifeline — never let a drop go uncaught.
tips: Multi-ball = more points per second, but harder to track — worth the risk.
A boosted wide paddle makes catching drops and deflecting misses much easier.
Prioritize bricks in the lowest rows to push back the encroaching wave.

visual.powerupHint: Shoot a special asteroid to collect its power-up

step0.title: Welcome to Asteroids
step0.description: Fly your ship through a field of tumbling asteroids and blast them apart before they hit you. Survive as long as possible, build your score, and watch out — the further you go, the faster and thicker they come.
tips: You start with 3 lives. Hitting an asteroid costs one, and you flash invincible for 2 seconds after.
Asteroids wrap off the edges of the canvas — they respawn on the opposite side.
The game has no end state other than running out of lives — just push for a new high score.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Move with WASD or arrow keys and aim with the mouse — click or hold the left mouse button to shoot. On mobile, the left on-screen joystick thrusts your ship and the right one aims and fires while held.
tips: WASD / arrows move in the direction you press, regardless of which way you're facing.
Mouse aim is always active on desktop — you don't need to hold any key to steer.
Right joystick: push and hold in any direction to both aim and auto-fire simultaneously.

step2.title: Asteroid Sizes & Splitting
step2.description: Large asteroids split into two medium ones when shot. Mediums split into two smalls. Smalls vanish entirely. Each split scores points, with small asteroids worth the most. Large asteroids can also carry special power-up icons inside them.
tips: Large = 20 pts, Medium = 50 pts, Small = 100 pts — shoot the chain all the way through.
A single large asteroid can create up to 4 small ones — each worth 100 pts.
Small asteroids move fastest and are the trickiest to hit under pressure.

step3.title: Power-Ups
step3.description: Some large asteroids have a glowing symbol inside them. Shoot and destroy that asteroid to instantly collect the power-up. Each one lasts a limited time — stack them wisely for maximum effect.
tips: + Extra Life: one of the rarest drops — always prioritise shooting it.
⚡ Rapid Fire + ◈ Spread Shot together create a devastating triple-burst — a strong combo.
🛡 Shield absorbs one hit completely and expires — it does not stack.
×2 Multiplier lasts 15 seconds and doubles all points earned — save it for dense asteroid clusters.
Power-ups respawn on the asteroid even if you miss — they're only collected on final destruction.

step4.title: Shooting Mechanics
step4.description: Your ship fires one bullet at a time at a 0.2 s interval. Rapid Fire halves that to 0.1 s. Spread Shot fires three bullets in a fan pattern — left, center, and right — letting you cover a wider area at once.
tips: Bullets travel at a fixed speed and disappear after 1.5 seconds — don't waste shots across the map.
Spread Shot is especially effective against tight clusters and fast small asteroids.
Combining Rapid Fire with Spread Shot fires 3-bullet bursts at double speed — almost unstoppable.

step5.title: Scoring & Difficulty
step5.description: Points come from destroying asteroids — multiply them with the ×2 power-up for maximum gain. Every 500 points increases the difficulty level, making asteroids spawn faster and speed up. The score multiplier resets to ×1 after 15 seconds.
tips: Difficulty grows as 1 + floor(score / 500) × 0.3 — score 2000 and spawn rate nearly doubles.
Collect the ×2 multiplier right before a large wave for the biggest point burst.
Don't chase asteroids off-screen — new ones spawn continuously at the edges.

visual.timerNote: ⏱ Run out of time = lose a life
visual.clearNote: ✓ Eat everything to advance to next level

step0.title: Welcome to Pac-Man
step0.description: Navigate a randomly generated maze, eat every food dot and power pellet to complete the level. Four coloured ghosts hunt you down — avoid them unless you're powered up. You have 60 seconds and 3 lives.
tips: Each level generates a fresh maze — layouts change every time.
The camera shows the full board; plan a route before ghosts close in.
Clearing every dot and pellet triggers a level-complete animation, then the next level starts.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Use the arrow keys or WASD to move Pac-Man through the maze. Your input is buffered — press the next direction just before a corner and Pac-Man will turn as soon as the path opens. You cannot reverse into the direction you just came from.
tips: Pre-queue your next turn: tap the direction key a moment before the junction.
The buffer holds up to 2 inputs — spam doesn't help, but early input does.
On mobile, use the on-screen D-pad. Touch precision matters more in tight corridors.

step2.title: Food & Power-Ups
step2.description: Small yellow dots are food (10 pts each). Larger glowing pellets are power-ups (20 pts). Eating a power pellet adds 15 seconds to the clock, activates 8-second power mode where ghosts turn scared and blue, and starts the countdown to score bonus ghost kills. Eat all food and pellets to finish the level.
tips: There are exactly 4 power pellets per level — use them when ghosts are clustered nearby.
Time is your biggest enemy early on — prioritise clearing dots quickly over chasing ghosts.
Power mode lasts only 8s; plan your ghost hunt before activating the pellet.

step3.title: Ghosts
step3.description: Ghosts chase you directly 85% of the time and wander randomly the other 15%. During power mode they turn blue and scared — run into them to earn 200 pts each. After being eaten a ghost fades out and respawns 5 seconds later in a random location.
tips: Ghost speed increases +0.15 per level — early levels are forgiving, later ones are not.
Eating a ghost teleports it to a random safe spot; it cannot immediately re-catch you.
After taking a hit you get 2 seconds of invincibility — use that window to escape.

step4.title: Portals
step4.description: Each maze has two portal pairs: a horizontal pair on the left and right walls (at a random row), and a vertical pair on the top and bottom walls (at a random column). Walk into a purple edge to instantly teleport to the matching edge on the opposite side.
tips: Ghosts also use portals — don't assume the exit side is safe before you jump.
Portals are great escape routes when a ghost is blocking your direct path.
Portal positions change every level, so check the edges at the start of each maze.

step5.title: Scoring & Levels
step5.description: Points come from food dots (10), power pellets (20), and scared ghosts (200). The level counter never stops — each level speeds up the ghosts slightly and shrinks the grid cell size down to a minimum. You start with 3 lives; a life is lost when a ghost catches you or the timer hits zero.
tips: Ghost count scales every 5 levels: levels 1–4 have 2 ghosts, level 6 adds a third, and so on up to 7.
Lost a life? All ghosts are instantly repositioned randomly so you can recover safely.
High scores are saved automatically — beat your personal best to submit a new one.

visual.bombBlock: Placed bombs block your own path
visual.dropChance: 30% drop chance when a block is destroyed

step0.title: Welcome to Bomberman
step0.description: Move your white astronaut through a grid-based map and plant bombs to destroy soft orange blocks and enemies. Clear every enemy to advance to the next level. The map grows denser and enemies grow faster with each level.
tips: Hard purple walls are indestructible — only the orange blocks can be blown up.
You always start at position (1,1) in the top-left safe zone.
The bottom-left corner of the canvas shows your remaining bomb count and current blast radius.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Use arrow keys or WASD to move. Press Space (or the 💣 button on mobile) to place a bomb at your current tile. Hold a direction key to keep moving — the player steps once every 180ms. You cannot walk through a bomb you have already placed.
tips: Place a bomb, then walk away — you cannot detonate early, the fuse is always 2 seconds.
You can walk over the tile where you placed a bomb immediately, but not re-enter it afterward.
On mobile the D-pad and round bomb button work exactly like keyboard controls.

step2.title: Bombs & Explosions
step2.description: Each bomb explodes after a 2-second fuse, sending a blast arm in all 4 directions for a number of cells equal to your current radius (starts at 1). Blasts are blocked by indestructible walls. Destructible blocks stop the arm and get destroyed. Explosions last 420ms — avoid those cells!
tips: Chain reactions: a bomb caught in another explosion detonates instantly — great for combos.
Your own explosion can kill you — always have an escape tile ready before placing.
The blast arm travels through empty cells but stops at the first destructible block it hits.

step3.title: Blocks & Power-Ups
step3.description: Destroying a soft block awards 10 pts and has a 30% chance of dropping a power-up. Yellow circles give an extra bomb slot (up to 5). Pink circles increase your blast radius by 1 (up to 5). Red circles give you an extra life. Walk over a power-up to collect it for +50 pts.
tips: Prioritise Radius (pink) power-ups early — a wider blast makes clearing enemies much faster.
Extra bomb capacity (yellow) lets you cover more area before waiting for fuses to expire.
Life power-ups (red) are rare — about a 10% share of all drops. Grab them whenever they appear.

step4.title: Enemies
step4.description: Enemies come in 5 visual variants but share the same AI: they chase you based on a probability that grows each level — 24% at level 1, reaching a cap of 70% above level 12. The rest of the time they wander randomly. Enemy speed also increases +0.15 per level.
tips: Funnel enemies into a corridor, place a bomb at the entrance, and retreat — reliable kill.
Enemies cannot move through placed bombs, so use bombs as temporary walls to buy time.
Killing all enemies clears the level immediately — you don't need to destroy every block.

step5.title: Scoring & Levels
step5.description: Points come from destroying soft blocks (10), picking up power-ups (50), and killing enemies (100). Each level adds more enemies — one new enemy every 2 levels up to a maximum of 10. Destructible block density also increases 3% per level up to 45%. You have 3 lives and get 1.5s of invincibility after each hit.
tips: Enemy count formula: 1 + floor((level-1)/2), capped at 10. Level 9 is the first 5-enemy stage.
Grid cell size shrinks slightly each level (30px → min 14px), making navigation tighter.
High scores save automatically — your best score, level reached, and bombs placed are all tracked.

visual.hitboxNote: 2px inset hitbox — tighter than it looks
visual.movingChanceNote: 30% of pipes will move beyond score 5

step0.title: Welcome to Bird
step0.description: Flap your rectangular bird through the gaps between pipe pairs. Each pipe you clear scores one point. Hit a pipe, the ceiling, or the floor and it's game over. The game runs continuously — there are no levels, just how far you can go.
tips: The bird starts at the vertical center and immediately begins falling — flap straight away.
Gravity is constant at 0.08 per frame; each flap sets velocity to +3 for a strong upward kick.
The bird rotates with velocity: nose-up on flap, nose-down as it falls — use this as a visual cue.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: There is only one input: flap. Press Space or the Up arrow on keyboard, click or tap the canvas, or press the large Flap button below the canvas. Every input gives the bird the same upward velocity burst. On game over, the same input restarts.
tips: Short taps give smaller altitude gains — use quick taps to thread tight gaps.
Holding the button does nothing extra; it's a single impulse per press.
On mobile the Flap button is large enough to hit reliably with a thumb.

step2.title: Pipes & Collision
step2.description: Each pipe pair has a top pipe and a bottom pipe with a gap between them. The gap starts at 100px wide and shrinks by 1px for every 5 points scored, down to a minimum of 70px. Each pipe is 50px wide. The collision hitbox is 2px inset on all sides of the bird — slightly more forgiving than the visible square.
tips: Aim for the vertical center of the gap — the 2px inset gives you a small margin on tight pipes.
Pipes pass at the same speed they spawn; there's no acceleration within a single pipe.
A pipe is counted as passed as soon as its right edge clears the bird's x position.

step3.title: Moving Pipes
step3.description: After you score 5 points, each new pipe has a 30% chance of oscillating vertically. Moving pipes bob up and down using a sine wave — their gap shifts continuously. A red dot in the centre of the gap marks any moving pipe so you can spot it early.
tips: Watch for the red dot as the pipe enters from the right — it gives you time to adjust altitude.
Moving pipes have the same speed and gap size rules as static ones; only the gap position changes.
At high scores, moving pipes can stack up back-to-back — stay near the centre and make small corrections.

step4.title: Themes & Difficulty
step4.description: The sky, pipe, and bird colours blend smoothly between 5 themes, rotating every 10 points. This is purely visual — a nice way to track rough progress. Difficulty comes from three simultaneous escalations: gap size shrinks, pipe speed increases, and new pipes spawn more frequently.
tips: Theme 5 (dark grey sky) appears around score 40 — reaching it means you're playing well.
Speed formula: baseSpeed (2.0) + score × 0.01. At score 50 that's 2.5 — noticeably faster.
Spawn interval: max(100, 140 − floor(score/3)) frames. Score 12 tightens it from 140 to 100.

step5.title: Scoring
step5.description: You score 1 point every time a pipe pair fully passes your bird. There are no bonus points or multipliers — just how many pipes you clear. Your high score is saved automatically and submitted to the leaderboard. The game resets on death; there is no pause.
tips: Consistency beats aggression — maintaining a mid-height position is safer than chasing the exact gap centre.
At score 30+ the gap is 94px and pipes spawn every ~105 frames — start flying conservatively.
Moving pipes become the main threat past score 20. Treat the red dot as an early warning and adjust before you reach it.

step0.title: Welcome to Minesweeper
step0.description: A grid of hidden cells conceals a set number of mines. Your goal is to reveal every safe cell without detonating a single mine. The faster you clear the board, the higher your score multiplier.
tips: Grid size and mine count are fully customisable before each game.
Your high score is saved automatically after each win.
Mines are always placed after your first click — you can never lose immediately.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: On PC, left-click a cell to reveal it and right-click to place or remove a flag. On mobile, tap a cell to reveal it — or activate Flag Mode using the 🚩 button below the board, then tap to flag.
tips: On PC, right-click any unrevealed cell to flag or unflag it instantly — no button needed.
On mobile, the 🚩 button glows red when Flag Mode is active — tap it again to go back to reveal mode.
Flagged cells cannot be accidentally revealed, even if you tap them.

step2.title: Cells & Numbers
step2.description: Hidden cells appear as raised dark squares. Revealed cells are flat and darker. A number tells you exactly how many mines are touching that cell across its 8 neighbours — this is your main clue for deduction.
step2.colorHint: Each number has a unique colour to help you read the board at a glance.
tips: A '1' next to a single unrevealed neighbour means that cell is definitely a mine — flag it.
Higher numbers like 3–5 mark dense mine zones — be extra careful near them.
Revealed '0' (empty) cells cascade automatically, opening large safe regions in one click.

step3.title: Flags & Mines
step3.description: Use flags (🚩) to mark cells you suspect are mines. This prevents accidental reveals and helps track which mines you've accounted for. If you click a mine (💣) without flagging it, the game ends immediately.
tips: Flag every cell you're certain is a mine before clicking its neighbours.
On mobile, the 🚩 button below the board switches between reveal and flag mode.
Flags are free to place and remove — use them to map out dangerous zones.

step4.title: Cascade Reveals
step4.description: Clicking an empty cell (0) automatically reveals all adjacent cells. If those are also empty, the cascade continues outward — a single click can clear a large section of the board at once.
step4.hint: Clicking a '0' cell opens all connected empty cells automatically.
tips: Look for corners or edges where a 0 cell might cascade across a large safe area.
Cascades also reveal the numbered border cells, giving you more deduction information.
After a big cascade, quickly scan the new numbers — they often reveal safe next moves.

step5.title: Grid Customisation
step5.description: Before starting, you can set the number of rows, columns, and mines in the header inputs. Rows and columns range from 5 to 20, and mines must be at least 1 and fewer than the total cell count. Settings lock while a game is running.
step5.hint: Larger grids with more mines score higher but require more careful play.
tips: Start with 10 × 10 and 10 mines for a balanced beginner experience.
Grid settings are locked during a game — choose your difficulty before pressing Play.
Higher mine density leaves less empty space to cascade, making the game significantly harder.

step6.title: Scoring & Time Multiplier
step6.description: You earn 1 point per revealed cell, plus a +100 bonus for winning. Your final score is then multiplied by a time bonus — the faster you clear the board, the higher the multiplier, up to 4× for very fast clears.
tips: Finishing in under 30 seconds awards the maximum 4× multiplier.
Large cascades reveal many cells at once — they're your best tool for a fast clear.
Hitting a mine ends the game with no multiplier — accuracy matters more than speed.

step0.title: Welcome to 2048
step0.description: Slide tiles on a 4×4 grid to merge matching numbers. Each merge doubles the tile value — keep combining until you reach the golden 2048 tile to win. The higher you go, the more points you earn.
tips: Every move spawns a new tile (90% chance of 2, 10% chance of 4).
Plan several moves ahead — a single bad slide can fill the board faster than expected.
Your high score is saved automatically whenever you beat it.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: On PC, use the arrow keys to slide all tiles in that direction. On mobile, swipe anywhere on the board. The D-pad buttons below the board work on both PC and mobile for precise taps.
step1.dpadHint: The D-pad below the board works on both PC and mobile.
tips: Arrow keys on PC move all tiles at once — hold briefly to repeat.
On mobile, swipe anywhere on the canvas in any direction.
The on-screen D-pad is great for precise single moves on touch devices.

step2.title: Merging Tiles
step2.description: When two tiles with the same value collide in a slide, they merge into one tile worth their sum. Merging earns you points equal to the new tile's value. Each tile can only merge once per move.
step2.hint: Slide left: two 2-tiles collapse into a single 4-tile, earning +4 points.
tips: A tile can only merge once per slide — two merges in the same row won't chain.
Planning merges along a single edge keeps high-value tiles from getting stranded.
Every merge adds the resulting value to your score — bigger tiles = bigger rewards.

step3.title: Tile Progression
step3.description: Tiles progress from 2 all the way up to 2048 and beyond. Lower tiles (2 and 4) are beige; tiles from 8 to 64 shift to warm oranges; tiles from 128 onward turn golden. The 2048 tile is the brightest gold — your goal.
step3.hint: Colour is a quick way to judge a tile's value at a glance.
tips: Keep your highest-value tile in a corner — it's easier to build around.
Avoid scattering high tiles across the board; merge them toward one edge.
Tiles above 2048 exist if you keep playing after winning — the game doesn't stop.

step4.title: Earning Power-ups
step4.description: Three special power-ups are unlocked automatically when you merge tiles to specific milestones. Each type is capped at 2 uses at a time — earn more by hitting the milestone again.
step4.hint: Merging 32+32=64 gives Remove, 128+128=256 gives Double, 512+512=1024 gives Shuffle.
tips: 🗑️ Remove is earned by merging to 64 — max 2 at a time.
✖️ Double is earned by merging to 256 — doubles a tile's value and adds it to your score.
🔀 Shuffle is earned by merging to 1024 — randomly repositions all tiles on the board.

step5.title: Using Power-ups
step5.description: Click (or tap) a power-up button to activate it. Remove and Double then wait for you to tap a tile on the board to apply the effect. Shuffle activates instantly. Press ESC or the ESC button to cancel a pending Remove or Double.
step5.removeDesc: Tap a tile to erase it
step5.doubleDesc: Tap a tile to double it
step5.escHint: Cancels a pending Remove or Double
tips: Use Remove to clear a low-value tile that's blocking a merge you need.
Use Double on your highest tile for a massive score and merge opportunity.
Shuffle is a last resort — use it when the board is locked with no useful moves left.

step6.title: Scoring & Winning
step6.description: Your score grows with every merge — the new tile's value is added each time. Reach the 2048 tile to win. The game ends when the board is full and no adjacent tiles can merge.
tips: High-value merges (like 128+128=256) are worth far more than chains of small merges.
You can keep playing after hitting 2048 to chase even higher tiles and scores.
Power-ups can rescue a full board — keep some in reserve for emergencies.

step0.title: Welcome to Sudoku
step0.description: Fill every cell in the grid so that each row, column, and box contains every number exactly once. Some cells are pre-filled as clues — you fill in the rest. Complete the whole puzzle without running out of lives to win.
tips: The default grid is 9×9 (subgrid size 3), but you can change it before starting.
Every valid puzzle has exactly one solution — no guessing required.
Your high score is saved automatically after each completed puzzle.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Click or tap a cell to select it (it highlights in pink). Then type a number on your keyboard, or tap a number from the pad below the board. Press Delete, Backspace, or 0 to erase a cell.
tips: On PC, click a cell and type the number directly — no need to use the on-screen pad.
On mobile, tap the cell first, then tap a number from the pad below the board.
Pressing 0, Delete, or Backspace clears the selected cell's value and any pencil notes.

step2.title: The Rules
step2.description: Each row must contain every number from 1 to N with no repeats. Each column must also contain every number exactly once. And each bold-bordered box must contain every number once too — all three constraints must hold at the same time.
tips: If a number already appears in a row, it can't go anywhere else in that row.
Boxes are the bold-bordered subgrids — in a 9×9 puzzle each box is 3×3.
When a cell has only one possible number given all three constraints, fill it in immediately.

step3.title: Cell Colours
step3.description: Given (fixed) cells show in grey — you can't change them. Numbers you enter correctly turn blue. If you place a number that already exists in the same row, column, or box, the cell turns red to warn you — and you lose a life.
tips: Grey cells are the puzzle's given clues — they can never be changed.
Blue means your number is correct and doesn't conflict with any constraint.
A red cell warns you of a conflict and costs a life — remove the number to stop the penalty.

step4.title: Pencil Mode & Eraser
step4.description: Activate the Pencil button (it glows pink) to jot small candidate numbers inside a cell without committing to them. This is useful for tracking possibilities. The Eraser button clears both the cell's value and any pencil notes at once.
tips: Pencil notes don't trigger the duplicate check — they're never treated as answers.
Tap Pencil again, or press the Eraser, to switch back to normal input mode.
Pencil notes are automatically cleared when you fill in the cell with a real number.

step5.title: Lives & Difficulty
step5.description: You start with 3 lives shown as hearts. Placing a number that conflicts with an existing row, column, or box costs one life. Lose all three and the game ends. Difficulty controls how many cells are pre-filled: Easy gives the most clues, Hard gives the fewest.
tips: The same conflict on the same cell won't punish you twice — remove it and try another number.
Easy mode gives ~45% of cells, Hard gives only ~5% — Hard is extremely sparse.
Keeping all 3 lives intact gives a +15% bonus to your final score.

step6.title: Grid Size
step6.description: Before starting, set the subgrid size (2–5) in the header. This controls the full board: subgrid 2 = 4×4, subgrid 3 = 9×9, subgrid 4 = 16×16, subgrid 5 = 25×25. Larger grids are much harder but score significantly more points.
step6.hint: Set the subgrid size before pressing Play — it locks once the game starts.
tips: Start with subgrid 2 (4×4) to learn the rules, then work up to the classic 9×9.
Subgrid 4 and 5 are expert territory — numbers go up to 16 or 25.
Grid settings are locked during a game — choose your size before pressing Play.

step7.title: Scoring
step7.description: Your score is calculated when you complete the puzzle: 10 × gridSize² × time multiplier × lives factor × difficulty factor. Finishing faster, keeping more lives, and playing on a harder difficulty all increase your final score.
tips: Time multiplier goes from 4× (under 10 minutes) down to 1× — every second counts.
Each life you keep adds ~5% to the lives factor — a perfect run gives +15%.
Hard difficulty applies a ×1.15 bonus; Easy applies ×0.9 — the same puzzle scores more on Hard.

step0.title: Welcome to Solitaire
step0.description: Choose from three classic modes before starting: Klondike (the timeless 7-column game), Spider (a double-deck challenge across 10 columns), or FreeCell (all cards face-up with 4 temporary holding cells). Each mode has its own rules and scoring.
tips: Select your game mode before pressing Play — it can't be changed mid-game.
Klondike is the classic starting point; FreeCell is highly strategic; Spider is the hardest.
All modes track your score, time, and move count for multiplier bonuses.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Click or tap a card to select it (it highlights in gold). Then click or tap a valid destination to move it. On PC you can also drag and drop cards directly. An Undo button appears whenever there is history to revert — use it freely.
tips: A gold border appears on the selected card — tap any valid spot to place it.
Undo is unlimited and free — use it to explore different paths without penalty.
On mobile, dragging is smoother for multi-card moves in Klondike and Spider.

step2.title: Klondike Layout
step2.description: Seven tableau columns are dealt at the start: column 1 gets 1 card, column 2 gets 2, and so on up to 7. Only the top card of each column is face-up. The remaining cards form the deck (top-left); clicking the deck turns cards to the waste pile (next to it). Four foundation slots sit top-right.
tips: Clicking the deck reveals the top card to the waste pile — only the top waste card can be played.
When the deck is empty, click the empty deck to recycle the waste pile back.
Face-down cards in the tableau flip automatically when they become the top card.

step3.title: Tableau Rules
step3.description: In Klondike and FreeCell, cards stack in descending rank with alternating colours — a red 7 goes on a black 8, a black 6 on a red 7, and so on. In Spider, suit colour doesn't matter, only rank order. Only a King can start a new empty column.
step3.altHint: Black 8 → Red 7 → Black 6: alternating colours, descending rank
tips: Alternating colour is required in Klondike and FreeCell — same-colour stacks are not allowed.
Spider only requires descending rank; suit doesn't matter unless you want a completed run.
Moving a King to an empty column opens a strategic gap — use it wisely.

step4.title: Foundation Piles
step4.description: Cards go to foundations starting with Ace and ascending by rank within the same suit, all the way to King. In Klondike and FreeCell there are 4 foundations (one per suit). In Spider, completing a full 13-card same-suit run in the tableau sends it to a foundation automatically.
step4.hint: Build each suit Ace → 2 → 3 → … → King in the matching foundation slot.
tips: You can move a card from the foundation back to the tableau if you need it — but it costs points.
In Spider, a completed run (K down to A in one suit) leaves the tableau automatically.
Filling a foundation suit earns a +50 bonus on top of the standard +15 per card.

step5.title: Spider Mode
step5.description: Spider uses two full decks across 10 tableau columns. All cards start face-down except the top of each column. There is no waste pile — instead, clicking the deck deals one face-up card to every column at once. Complete a full King-to-Ace run of the same suit to send it to a foundation.
tips: Deal from the deck only when you're truly stuck — it can disrupt sequences you've built.
Any rank can go on an empty column in Spider, unlike Klondike's Kings-only rule.
Try to keep sequences in the same suit from the start — mixed suits can't complete a foundation run.

step6.title: FreeCell Mode
step6.description: All 52 cards are dealt face-up across 8 tableau columns — nothing is hidden. Four free cells (top-left, pink-bordered) let you temporarily park one card each. Use them as a buffer to unblock key moves. The four foundations work exactly as in Klondike: Ace up to King by suit.
tips: Free cells are precious — parking a card there earns +5 points but blocks that slot.
All cards are visible from the start, so FreeCell is almost entirely a puzzle of planning.
Nearly every FreeCell deal is solvable; if you're stuck, undo and try a different order.

step7.title: Scoring & Multipliers
step7.description: Points are earned with each move. When you win, the raw score is multiplied by the average of a time multiplier (faster = higher) and a moves multiplier (fewer moves = higher). Both multipliers range from 1.0× to 3.0×/2.5×.
tips: Foundation moves are worth 3× tableau moves — prioritise them when possible.
Fewer total moves boost the moves multiplier more than finishing quickly boosts the time multiplier.
Completing a full foundation suit earns +50 on top of the 13 × +15 card bonus.

step0.title: Welcome to Checkers
step0.description: Standard 8×8 checkers. Red pieces start at the bottom, Black pieces at the top. Pieces only ever sit on dark squares. Red always moves first. Capture all your opponent's pieces — or leave them with no legal move — to win.
tips: Only dark squares are used — pieces never touch light squares.
Red always goes first regardless of which colour you're assigned.
A coin toss at the start of each game decides which colour you play.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Click or tap a piece to select it — valid destination squares light up with a pink dot. Then click or tap a highlighted square to move. You have 20 seconds per move; if time runs out, a random legal move is made for you automatically.
step1.timerHint: 20 s per move — random move on timeout
tips: Pink dots mark empty squares you can move to; pink borders mark enemy pieces you can capture.
Clicking a different friendly piece while one is selected will switch your selection.
The 20-second timer resets after every move, including the CPU's.

step2.title: Pieces & Movement
step2.description: Regular pieces move diagonally forward one square at a time — Red moves up the board, Black moves down. Pieces can only land on dark squares. Kings (earned by reaching the opposite back rank) move diagonally in any direction.
step2.darkOnly: Pieces only ever occupy dark squares
tips: Red moves toward row 0 (top), Black moves toward row 7 (bottom).
Regular pieces can only move forward — they can never retreat without becoming a King.
Kings are the most powerful pieces; protecting them while creating your own is key.

step3.title: Captures
step3.description: To capture an opponent's piece, jump diagonally over it to the empty square directly behind it. The captured piece is removed from the board. A pink border highlights enemy pieces you can jump over when one of your pieces is selected.
step3.hint: Red jumps diagonally over Black and lands two squares away.
tips: Captures are diagonal jumps — you must land on the empty square immediately past the enemy.
You can capture forwards or backwards with a King, but only forward with a regular piece.
Setting up a capture by moving a piece into range is often called a 'sacrifice' — use it carefully.

step4.title: Must-Jump & Multi-Jump
step4.description: If any of your pieces can make a capture, you must capture — you cannot make a regular move instead. A yellow ring highlights the piece you are forced to use. If after a capture another jump is available with the same piece, you must keep jumping in the same turn (multi-jump chain).
tips: Always scan the board for forced jumps before planning a regular move.
Multi-jump chains can remove several pieces in one turn — they're game-changing.
Becoming newly kinged ends your turn even if another jump was available.

step5.title: King Promotion
step5.description: When a regular piece reaches the opponent's back rank — row 0 for Red, row 7 for Black — it is crowned a King and gains a ♛ symbol. Kings can then move and capture in all four diagonal directions, making them far more flexible than regular pieces.
tips: Rushing to promote pieces early can open winning lines — but don't leave your back rank empty.
A King at the centre of the board controls far more squares than one near the edge.
If you become a King during a jump, your turn ends immediately — no chain continues.

step6.title: Game Modes & Difficulty
step6.description: CPU mode lets you play against the computer at four difficulty levels, using a minimax AI with increasing search depth. Online mode matches you against a real opponent via ELO-based matchmaking — both players get a 20-second move timer. A coin toss assigns colours at the start of every game.
step6.coinToss: Coin toss decides your colour each game
tips: Easy CPU plays randomly — great for learning. Grandmaster looks 6 moves ahead.
In Online mode, forfeit is available if you need to leave mid-game.
CPU games don't affect your ELO rating — only Online games count.

step7.title: Winning & ELO
step7.description: You win by capturing all of your opponent's pieces, or by leaving them with no legal move. Online games update your ELO rating — wins earn points based on your opponent's rating, losses subtract points. Higher-rated opponents give more ELO for a win and less for a loss.
tips: Leaving an opponent with no legal moves is just as valid a win as capturing everything.
A draw is possible if both players agree or no progress is made — rare in standard play.
Focus on piece count advantage early, then use your King to mop up.

step0.title: Welcome to Chess
step0.description: Classic chess on an 8×8 board. White pieces start on ranks 1–2, Black on ranks 7–8. White always moves first. The goal is to checkmate your opponent's King — put it in a position where it is under attack and has no legal escape. The board uses standard algebraic notation (a–h files, 1–8 ranks).
tips: White always moves first — a coin toss decides which colour you play.
The board flips automatically so your pieces are always at the bottom.
Light squares are cream (#e8edf9) and dark squares are green (#779556) — classic tournament style.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Click or tap a piece to select it — it highlights in pink and legal destination squares show pink dots. Click or tap any highlighted square to move there. Clicking a different friendly piece switches the selection. You have 20 seconds per move; if time expires, a random legal move is made for you automatically.
step1.clickDest: Click a highlighted square to move
step1.tapDest: Tap a highlighted square to move
step1.timer: 20 s per move — random move on timeout
tips: Pink dots mark empty squares you can move to; a pink circle ring marks enemy pieces you can capture.
Clicking the same piece again deselects it — click a different friendly piece to switch.
The timer resets to 20 s after every move, including the CPU's response.

step2.title: Pieces & Movement
step2.description: Each piece type moves differently. The King (♔/♚) moves one square in any direction and must never step into check. The Queen (♕/♛) is the most powerful — it moves any distance in any direction. Rooks move in straight lines, Bishops diagonally, and Knights jump in an L-shape (2+1 squares), leaping over other pieces. Pawns move forward one square (two on their first move) and capture diagonally.
tips: Knights are the only pieces that can jump over others — use them to escape crowded positions.
Bishops are permanently locked to one square colour: light-squared or dark-squared.
Piece values (rough): Pawn=1, Knight=3, Bishop=3, Rook=5, Queen=9. The King is invaluable.

step3.title: Special Moves
step3.description: Three special moves add depth. Castling: the King slides two squares toward a Rook, and the Rook jumps to the other side — only if neither piece has moved and no squares between them are occupied or attacked. En passant: a Pawn that has just advanced two squares can be captured by an adjacent enemy Pawn as if it had moved only one — but only on the very next move. Promotion: a Pawn reaching the back rank is automatically promoted to a Queen.
step3.castleHint: King slides 2 sq, Rook jumps over
step3.epHint: Capture as if pawn moved 1 sq
tips: Castling simultaneously moves the King to safety and activates a Rook — do it early.
En passant is easy to forget — your opponent can legally skip it if not taken immediately.
Promotion is always to Queen here — in competitive chess you can promote to any piece.

step4.title: Check & Checkmate
step4.description: Your King is in check when an enemy piece attacks it — the King's square turns red. You must resolve check immediately: move the King, block the attack, or capture the attacking piece. If there is no legal way out, it is checkmate and the game ends. Putting your opponent in checkmate is the only way to win.
step4.checkHint: King square turns red — must escape
tips: You cannot move into check — any move that leaves your King in check is illegal.
Discovered check: moving one piece reveals an attack by another — very powerful.
Double check (two pieces attacking simultaneously) can only be resolved by moving the King.

step5.title: Draw Conditions
step5.description: A game can end in a draw without checkmate in four ways: Stalemate — a player has no legal moves but is not in check (the position above shows Black's King trapped with no legal moves). Insufficient material — neither side has enough pieces to force checkmate. The fifty-move rule — fifty moves with no capture or pawn move. Threefold repetition — the same position occurs three times.
step5.stalemateHint: No legal moves, not in check
step5.insufficientHint: K vs K, K+B vs K, etc.
step5.fiftyMoveHint: 50 moves: no capture or pawn move
tips: Stalemate is a common trap: cornering an enemy King without leaving it a move gives them a free draw.
A lone King vs King+Rook is a forced checkmate — but King+Bishop vs King is a draw.
Online games can end in a draw by disconnection or forfeit too.

step6.title: Game Modes & Difficulty
step6.description: CPU mode offers four difficulty levels. Easy plays random legal moves.
