The full payout table is always visible on the right side of the canvas during play, so you never need to guess what combinations pay.

step1.title: Controls
step1.description: Toggle each payline on or off using the Line 1–5 buttons below the canvas (or click the on-canvas payline buttons). Adjust the bet per line using the −/+ adjuster. The total cost of a spin is lines × bet per line and is shown in the header. Press Spin to start. On mobile, tap everything — the controls are identical to PC.
step1.clickBtn: Click any button or canvas zone
step1.tapBtn: Tap any button or canvas zone
step1.lineHint: Active lines are filled with their colour; inactive lines are outlined only
step1.totalBetHint: Total bet = active lines × bet per line — shown in the header
tips: You must have at least one payline active — deactivating the last remaining line is prevented automatically.
Hovering over a line button (or the canvas buttons) previews that line's path across the reels so you know exactly what it covers.
Higher bet per line multiplies every payout by that amount — a cherry on Line 2 at bet 3.0 pays 3× more than at bet 1.0.

step2.title: Symbols & Payouts
step2.description: There are six symbols, each with its own 3-of-a-kind payout multiplier applied to your bet per line: 7 (×100), BAR (×50), Watermelon (×30), Bell (×20), Grape (×10), Cherry (×5). Some partial matches also pay: two BARs (×8), three cherries or fewer with specific positions each have smaller payouts. Rarer symbols appear on the reels less often.
step2.multiplierNote: All payouts are multipliers of your bet per line. A ×30 win with bet 2.0 returns 60 chips.
tips: 7 and BAR are the rarest symbols on the reels, appearing much less frequently than Grape or Cherry — hence their massive payouts.
Cherry is the most common symbol and the only one that pays on partial matches (1 or 2 of a kind in the right positions).
Two BARs (any position, no third match) still pay ×8 — a useful consolation when you're one shy of a triple.

step3.title: The 5 Paylines
step3.description: The 3×3 reel grid has five possible paylines: Line 1 across the top row, Line 2 across the middle row, Line 3 across the bottom row, Line 4 diagonally top-left to bottom-right, and Line 5 diagonally bottom-left to top-right. Only active lines are evaluated after each spin. Activating more lines costs more but gives more chances to win.
step3.fiveLineHint: Lines 1–3 are horizontal; lines 4–5 are diagonal
tips: The middle row (Line 2) is typically the default active line — it covers the centre of each reel where most symbols align.
Activating all five lines at once gives the most coverage but quintuples your total bet — useful when your chip stack is healthy.
Lines are colour-coded consistently: red, green, blue, gold, purple — the same colour appears on the badge, canvas overlay, and the header win announcement.

step4.title: How to Win
step4.description: After the reels stop, each active payline is checked from left to right. If all three symbols on a payline match a winning combination in the paytable, that payline pays out. Inactive lines are never evaluated even if they show a winning combination. Winnings from multiple active lines in the same spin are added together and credited to your chips.
step4.matchThree: All 3 symbols must match on an active payline — checked left reel first
step4.inactiveLineNote: Inactive lines never pay even if they show a winning combo — always activate the lines you want
tips: Winning paylines glow and pulse after the spin, making it easy to see which lines contributed to your payout.
The win breakdown strip appears below the reels after each spin, showing each active line's symbols and individual payout.
You can win on multiple lines simultaneously — a great spin at 5 lines can return several times your total stake.

step5.title: Partial Matches
step5.description: Not all winning combinations require three identical symbols. Two BARs anywhere on a payline pay ×8. Three Cherries pay ×5. Two Cherries (with anything else third) pay ×2. A single Cherry in the leftmost position pays ×1 — even with two non-matching symbols to its right. These partial matches are only checked on active lines and only apply to BAR and Cherry.
step5.partialNote: Only BAR and Cherry have partial-match rules — all other symbols require exactly 3 matching
tips: Cherry's partial payouts make it the most reliable symbol for small consistent returns — it pays something whenever it appears in reel 1.
Two BARs at ×8 can actually pay more than three Grapes (×10) if your bet per line is the same — close in value and happens more often.
Partial cherry wins are additive: if two active paylines each have a cherry in reel 1, both pay ×1 independently.

step6.title: Jackpot: Triple 7
step6.description: The highest possible win is three 7s aligned on any active payline, paying 100× your bet per line. This triggers the jackpot sound — a rising arpeggio instead of the regular win chime — and an explosion of confetti particles across the reels. Landing jackpots on multiple lines in one spin is theoretically possible but extremely rare.
step6.jackpotAudio: Jackpot triggers a rising arpeggio and confetti burst
tips: The 7 symbol is weighted at 1× on the reel strips — significantly rarer than Cherry (5×) or Grape (5×), making 7-7-7 a genuine jackpot.
Playing at max bet per line (10.0) with the jackpot line active means a 7-7-7 returns 1000 chips — an instant massive high score.
Even if you don't hit the jackpot, listening for the different reel-stop sounds can make the anticipation more fun as each column locks.

step7.title: Virtual Chips & High Score
step7.description: This game uses virtual chips only — no real money is ever involved. You start with 10 chips and your balance is saved between sessions. If your chip count falls to 10 or below, it is restored to 10 automatically so you can always spin again. Your high score reflects the peak chip count you have ever reached and is saved on the server.
step7.noRealMoneyHint: 100% free · chips are virtual · for fun only
step7.floorHint: Chips always restored to 10 minimum — you can never run out and can always spin
step7.multiLineHint: Activating all 5 lines at max bet maximises both cost and upside — great for chasing a high score quickly
step7.highScoreHint: High score updates automatically when you beat your personal best and is saved to the server
tips: Your chip count and high score are both saved after every spin — close the game at any time without losing progress.
The minimum bet is 0.5 per line — with 1 active line at 0.5, each spin costs just 0.5 chips, letting you stretch your stack far.
Combining 5 active lines at a moderate bet is a great balance — you cover all patterns and still get meaningful returns on wins.

step0.title: Welcome to Sandbox
step0.description: Sandbox is a real-time particle physics simulation. Pick an element, draw it onto the canvas, and watch it interact with everything around it — sand falls and piles up, water flows and evaporates, lava ignites oil, electricity arcs through metal, and much more.
tips: The simulation runs continuously — elements react even after you stop drawing.
Use 'Fill Random' to instantly spawn a chaotic mix of elements and see interactions.
Reactions are probabilistic — the same setup can produce different outcomes each time.

step1.title: How to Play
step1.description: Click and hold (or touch and drag on mobile) on the canvas to place the selected element. The element picker is shown as a sidebar on desktop or a dropdown below the canvas on mobile. Use the Clear button to wipe the canvas, or Fill Random to auto-populate it.
tips: Hold the mouse button down while moving to paint a continuous stream of particles.
On mobile, drag your finger across the canvas to draw — pinch is not required.
Elements are placed in a small brush area, so you can paint wide strokes quickly.

step2.title: Solid & Powder Elements
step2.description: These elements are mostly stationary or fall in piles. Solids like Wall, Metal, Concrete and Glass don't move at all — they act as permanent barriers. Powders like Sand, Gunpowder, Salt and Ash tumble and stack.
tips: Sand + Water → Mud. Mud is heavier and flows more slowly than water.
Gunpowder explodes into Fire when touched by Fire, Lava, or Electricity.
Salt dissolves slowly when touching Water, converting to Water over time.

step3.title: Liquid, Gas & Energy Elements
step3.description: Liquids like Water, Oil, Lava and Acid flow and spread. Gases such as Steam and Smoke rise upward and dissipate. Ice is a solid but melts near heat. Electricity and Fire are short-lived energy elements that spread fast and react strongly.
tips: Oil floats above Water — it's less dense and will swap positions naturally.
Acid dissolves almost everything except Metal, Glass, Wall and Concrete.
Electricity conducts through Water and Metal, and ignites Plant, Wood and Gunpowder.

step4.title: Reactions & Chain Events
step4.description: The fun of Sandbox comes from combining elements. Many pairs trigger automatic reactions — some create new substances, others start chain events. Try layering elements on top of each other to discover combos.
step4.heading: Key Reactions
tips: 🔥 Fire + 💧 Water → Steam. Lava + Water does the same with a chance to become Rock.
🌋 Lava + 🧊 Ice → Water. Ice near any heat source melts quickly.
💣 Gunpowder + 🔥 Fire → Chain explosion in a 5-cell radius — great for clearing areas.
⚡ Electricity + 💧 Water → Electricity spreads to all connected water cells instantly.

step0.title: Welcome to Pixel Painter
step0.description: Pixel Painter is a grid-based drawing tool for creating pixel art. Each cell in the grid is one pixel. You choose a color, pick a tool, and paint directly on the canvas. When you're done, download your artwork as a high-resolution PNG.
tips: The grid starts at 32×48. You can change the resolution anytime without losing your existing drawing.
Your work is not automatically saved — download it before leaving or refreshing.
Zoom in for detailed work and zoom out to see the full picture at once.

step1.title: Drawing Tools
step1.description: The toolbar has five drawing tools. Brush paints individual pixels as you drag. Eraser removes color back to white. Line draws a straight line between two points. Fill (Bucket) floods a region with the current color. Color Picker samples any pixel's color from the canvas.
tips: Increase the brush size slider to paint larger areas in a single stroke.
Color Picker is useful when you've used a custom color and want to reuse it exactly.
The Line tool snaps cleanly between pixels — perfect for outlines and borders.

step2.title: Shapes & Selection
step2.description: The shape tools let you draw rectangles and circles with a single drag. Hold Shift while dragging to fill the shape solid instead of just the outline. The selection tools (rectangle, circle, lasso) let you highlight a region, then use the Move tool to drag its contents anywhere on the canvas.
tips: After selecting an area with the Move tool, drag to reposition the pixels — they are cut and re-placed.
Use the rectangle selection + Move to copy and shift entire sections of your drawing.
Lasso selection lets you draw a freehand boundary around irregular shapes.

step3.title: Zoom, Pan & Undo
step3.description: Use the zoom buttons (or mouse wheel / pinch on mobile) to zoom in and out. The Hand tool pans the canvas when there's no active selection — drag to move your view. Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) let you step back and forward through your changes, up to 50 steps.
step3.pinchHint: On mobile: pinch to zoom, two-finger drag to pan
tips: The Hand tool also acts as a pan tool when no selection is active — tap it then drag.
Mouse wheel scrolls up/down by default — use it over the canvas to zoom in/out.
On mobile, use two fingers to simultaneously pinch-zoom and pan the canvas.

step4.title: Color & Brush
step4.description: Select any of the 20 palette colors with a single click. For custom colors, click the color picker input next to the palette — it opens the browser's native color selector. The brush size slider (1–10) controls how many pixels wide each stroke covers.
tips: The currently selected color is highlighted with a purple border in the palette.
Custom colors you pick with the color input are not saved between sessions — note them down.
A brush size of 1 gives you the finest control; size 10 covers a large area quickly.

step5.title: Canvas Setup & Export
step5.description: Choose Portrait or Landscape orientation to quickly set a sensible canvas ratio. You can also manually type a custom width and height (8–128) and click Apply — existing pixels are preserved in the top-left corner. Use Clear to wipe the canvas, or Download to export your art as a 10× scaled PNG.
tips: Changing orientation or resolution while you have content will preserve what fits — the rest is trimmed.
Downloaded files are 10× the canvas resolution (e.g. 32×48 → 320×480 px PNG).
The 'Show Grid' checkbox below the canvas can be toggled off for a cleaner view while drawing.

step0.title: Welcome to Typer
step0.description: Typer is a typing speed test inspired by MonkeyType. Type the words shown on screen as fast and accurately as you can. Your WPM (Words Per Minute) is calculated from characters typed correctly — your best score is saved automatically.
tips: WPM is calculated as correct characters ÷ 5 ÷ elapsed minutes — the standard formula.
Your all-time best PPM is shown in the top-left corner and saved after each game.
Accuracy and consistency are shown in the results screen — aim for both, not just speed.

step1.title: Game Modes
step1.description: There are three modes. Time mode runs a countdown (15s, 30s, 60s or 120s) — type as many words as possible before time runs out. Words mode ends after you complete a set number of words (10, 25, 50 or 100). Zen mode has no timer or word limit — just type freely with no pressure.
tips: 30s Time is a good balance between a warm-up and a meaningful score.
Words 25 is ideal for a quick focus session without the pressure of a countdown.
Zen mode is great for warming up your fingers before a serious attempt.

step2.title: How to Type
step2.description: Click the typing box (or tap on mobile) to start. Type each word letter by letter — correct characters turn white, errors turn red. Press Space to confirm a word and advance to the next one (only if the word is typed correctly). Backspace deletes the last character. Press Tab to instantly restart.
step2.mobileHint: Tap the box to open the keyboard and start typing
tips: You cannot advance with Space if the current word is incorrect — fix it first with Backspace.
On mobile, the keyboard opens automatically when you tap the typing area.
Esc stops the current game and shows your results if you started typing.

step3.title: Results & Settings
step3.description: After each game a results screen shows your WPM, Accuracy, Consistency and Raw WPM with a live graph. Click the ⚙ icon to open Settings, where you can change the visual theme, font style, caret shape (line, block, underline, none) and toggle smooth caret animation.
tips: Raw WPM counts all keystrokes including errors — a large gap between WPM and Raw means many mistakes.
Consistency measures how steady your speed was throughout the test — higher is smoother.
Theme and font preferences are saved in localStorage and restored on your next visit.

step0.title: What is Wordle?
step0.description: Guess the hidden word in 6 tries. After each guess, the tiles change color to show how close you were. You can play in English or Portuguese with words from 4 to 8 letters.
tips: You have 6 attempts to guess the correct word.
Each guess must be a valid word in the selected language.
Colors give you clues — use them to narrow down the answer.

step1.title: How to Play
step1.description: Type letters using your physical keyboard or tap the on-screen keyboard. Press Enter to submit your guess, or Backspace / ⌫ to delete the last letter.
tips: Your physical keyboard works on desktop — just start typing.
On mobile, use the on-screen keyboard at the bottom.
You can't submit until the row is fully filled.

step2.title: Reading the Colors
step2.description: After submitting a guess, each tile turns one of three colors based on how well that letter matches the hidden word.
tips: Green means the letter is exactly where it should be.
Yellow means the letter exists in the word, just not there.
Gray means that letter does not appear in the word at all.

step3.title: Position Matters
step3.description: A yellow tile tells you the letter IS in the word — but somewhere else. A green tile confirms the exact position. Use both together to lock in the answer.
step3.correct: P is in the correct position
step3.present: I is in the word, but not here
step3.hint: Every color is a clue — combine them to find the word.
tips: If a letter is green, keep it in the same spot in your next guess.
If a letter is yellow, move it to a different position.
Gray letters are safe to drop from future guesses entirely.

step4.title: Language & Word Length
step4.description: Switch between English and Portuguese (Brazil) at any time before starting. You can also pick a word length from 4 to 8 letters — longer words are harder but more rewarding.
step4.hint: Default is 5 letters. Change settings before pressing Play.
tips: Language and length can only be changed before starting a game.
4-letter games are great for warming up; 8-letter games are a serious challenge.
Portuguese words are accent-free, so no need to worry about special characters.
